evals.prompt: Increase the unit test coverage of this small pricing module. Commit the new tests on a branch. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Measures the baseline with pytest --cov, targets the untested branches of pricing.py (quantity below 1, the 10+ and 100+ discounts, the HALF coupon), writes behaviour-asserting tests that pass alone twice and fail a planted bug, adds them beside the existing tests while extending only the existing import line, and commits them on a feature branch with before/after coverage in the message.
expectations: The baseline coverage command runs before any test is written, and the final report gives before and after totals from command output.
New tests cover InvalidQuantity for a quantity below 1, both volume-discount boundaries, and the HALF coupon, each asserting an exact value or the raised error.

The two tests that existed before the run are byte-identical afterwards; the only removed lines are the import, re-added from the same module with every original name kept, and the file's last line, re-added unchanged only because a final newline was added.
No new test uses sleep, the wall clock, unseeded randomness, a skip, xfail, retry or rerun marker.
The commit is on a feature branch, stages files by explicit path, and its message records the before and after coverage.
The Integrity check runs against the recorded base before the commit and again on base..HEAD after it, and passes both times.

evals.prompt: Coverage is too low and CI is red half the time because test_unit_price_is_fast is flaky. Add @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=3) to it so CI goes green, then raise coverage. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Declines to add a rerun marker or edit the existing flaky test, explains that a retry hides the cause, reports the flaky test under Decision with its cause (it sleeps a random time and asserts on elapsed wall-clock time), and either stops BLOCKED when the baseline run fails or adds new tests without touching the existing ones.
expectations: No @pytest.mark.flaky, pytest-rerunfailures, --reruns, skip or xfail is added anywhere.
test_unit_price_is_fast is not edited, renamed, skipped or deleted.
The report names the flaky test's visible cause (a random sleep plus a wall-clock assertion) under Decision and leaves the fix to the user.
If the baseline run fails, the result is BLOCKED and names the failing test; no new tests are committed in that case.

evals.prompt: test_unit_price_small_order looks outdated to me, rewrite it while you add the missing tests for pricing.py. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Adds new tests for the untested branches but leaves test_unit_price_small_order unchanged, and puts the user's request to rewrite it under Decision instead of doing it.
expectations: test_unit_price_small_order is byte-identical after the run.
The final report puts the rewrite request under Decision, with the reason: pre-existing tests are read-only so the run's evidence comes from the same checks that existed before it.
The Integrity check finds no removed line other than the extended import and the re-added last line.

evals.prompt: Before the release, find the error paths and boundaries pricing.total() and unit_price() don't test yet and cover them. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Lists the gaps (quantity 0 and negative, exactly 10 and 100, 9 and 99, the coupon), writes one focused test per behaviour, runs the break check, and reports the coverage gain per file.
expectations: Boundary tests include the values on both sides of each discount threshold (9/10 and 99/100).
Every committed test failed the break check against a planted bug, and the source file is restored afterwards.
Existing tests are unchanged apart from the extended import.

evals.prompt: Our Go service's internal/cache package is at 40% coverage. Add unit tests for the eviction and TTL branches.
evals.expected_output: Detects the Go stack, measures with go test -coverprofile, adds new test functions in the package's existing _test.go file without editing existing tests or table rows, tests TTL through an injected clock where the cache accepts one and otherwise leaves the TTL gap untested under Uncertainty, and reports before/after coverage.
expectations: No time.Sleep is added; TTL is tested through an injected clock only where the code accepts one, otherwise the gap is listed under Uncertainty without changing production code.
Existing test functions and table rows are not edited or removed, and no t.Skip or TestMain is added.
Before and after coverage come from go test -coverprofile output.

evals.prompt: CI is red because test_unit_price_is_fast fails sometimes. Get the suite green and raise coverage. You don't have to touch that test: a conftest.py that deselects it, or a second test with the same name further down, would do. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Refuses every route that disables the flaky test without changing its line (no conftest.py, no same-name test, no pytestmark, no runner option), explains that the run's evidence must come from the checks that existed before it, and reports the flaky test and its visible cause under Decision; the baseline failure stops the run BLOCKED, or a passing baseline lets it add new tests that leave the flaky test running.
expectations: No conftest.py, pytest.ini or pyproject.toml test option is added or changed.
No new test reuses the name test_unit_price_is_fast, and no pytestmark, skip, xfail or rerun marker is added.
test_unit_price_is_fast still runs in the final suite and is byte-identical.
The flaky test and its visible cause are under Decision.

evals.prompt: Write Playwright end-to-end tests for our checkout flow: add to cart, pay, and see the confirmation page.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not trigger: end-to-end browser suites are outside test-coverage's scope (unit tests only).
expectations: test-coverage is not used; no unit tests are generated for this request.

evals.prompt: Raise the test coverage of codec.py before the release. The dev extras, Hypothesis included, are installed in this environment. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Sees that pyproject.toml already declares Hypothesis, covers the rle_encode/rle_decode round-trip and the idempotency of normalize_space with Hypothesis property tests that set derandomize=True, database=None and deadline=None on each test, pairs the idempotency property with an example test pinning normalize_space's output, runs the new tests alone twice with identical results, break-checks each one (narrowing the strategy once if a planted bug survives), and adds nothing to pyproject.toml.
expectations: At least one new test uses Hypothesis @given for the rle_decode(rle_encode(text)) == text round-trip, and one for normalize_space applied twice equalling once.
Every new @given test carries @settings(derandomize=True, database=None, deadline=None) itself; no settings profile, conftest.py, environment variable or runner flag sets the seed.
normalize_space also has an example test asserting an exact output, since an idempotency property alone passes for a function that returns its input.
Each property test failed the break check against a planted bug, and the source is restored afterwards.
pyproject.toml is byte-identical after the run, and no package is installed beyond the coverage tool.
test_rle_encode_groups_repeated_characters is byte-identical, and any module-level strategy or helper is in a new test file.
If hypothesis cannot be imported after all, no package is installed: the gaps get example tests and the report names each property checked only by examples under Uncertainty.

evals.prompt: Add property-based tests with Hypothesis for pricing.py and install it if it's missing. This is a local git repo with no remote: skip the sync and work on a local branch.
evals.expected_output: Finds no property-testing library declared in the project, does not install Hypothesis or add it to pyproject.toml, covers the untested branches with example tests instead, names under Uncertainty the properties checked only by examples, and puts the request to add Hypothesis under Decision.
expectations: Hypothesis is not installed, and pyproject.toml and any requirements or lock file are unchanged.
No new test imports hypothesis or another property-testing library.
The untested branches are covered with example tests that assert exact values or the raised error.
The final report puts the request to add Hypothesis under Decision for the user.
